skill.name: rivet-actors
skill.description: Reference guidance and runnable examples for building stateful applications with Rivet Actors, clients, workflows, authentication, storage, and realtime communication.
skill.summary: Build and troubleshoot Rivet Actors applications with focused documentation and TypeScript examples.
skill.author: rivet-dev

security_audit.summary: The review confirmed an unsigned JWT authorization bypass and a user-controlled outbound request that can enable SSRF. It also found multiple placeholder token validators that accept any nonempty value. The remaining static matches are documentation links, local endpoints, template strings, actor keys, or normal configuration patterns.

remediation.issue: The JWT example decodes claims without verifying the signature.
remediation.suggestion: Use a maintained JWT library and validate signature, algorithm, issuer, audience, expiry, and required claims before creating connection state.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends requests to queue-supplied URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist schemes and hosts, reject private and link-local addresses, resolve DNS safely, and apply outbound network restrictions.

remediation.issue: Several token validators accept any nonempty token.
remediation.suggestion: Replace placeholder validators with explicit mocks that fail by default, and label insecure examples beside every runnable implementation.

semantic_findings.title: Placeholder Token Validators Accept Any Nonempty Value
semantic_findings.description: Several runnable authentication examples treat any nonempty token as valid. Copying these validators into a deployed actor would allow unauthorized connections.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited validator directly returns success based only on token length. The educational context is clear, but the authentication behavior is definitively incomplete.

high_findings.title: Base64 decode
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The authentication function only decodes the JWT payload and never verifies its signature. An attacker can forge role and permission claims to bypass authorization.

high_findings.title: Fetch API call
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow fetches a URL supplied through a queue message without scheme, host, or private-network validation. A caller able to enqueue tasks could trigger SSRF.

content.value_statement: Stateful distributed applications require careful coordination, persistence, and realtime communication. This skill provides Rivet Actors guidance and runnable TypeScript examples.
actual_capabilities: Explains actor state, actions, keys, lifecycle hooks, connections, and destruction.
Provides TypeScript client examples for JavaScript, React, HTTP, WebSocket, and gateway access.
Shows authentication, access control, validation, error handling, and connection state patterns.
Demonstrates actor queues, workflows, scheduling, orchestration, and inter-actor communication.
Covers KV storage, SQLite persistence, migrations, metadata, and state synchronization.
Documents registry configuration, endpoints, CORS, regions, runtime modes, and deployment checks.
limitations: The skill provides documentation and examples, but it does not deploy or operate Rivet infrastructure.
Several authentication examples are simplified and require production security libraries and validation.
Example endpoints and credentials are placeholders that must be replaced with trusted configuration.
Workflow SDK material is beta content and may change with upstream releases.

use_cases.title: Create a Stateful Service
use_cases.description: Design actor state, actions, keys, and lifecycle behavior for a new TypeScript service.

use_cases.title: Add Realtime React Features
use_cases.description: Connect a React interface to actors, subscribe to events, and manage connection parameters.

use_cases.title: Design Durable Orchestration
use_cases.description: Combine queues, workflows, SQLite, and actor communication for resilient background processing.

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Actor
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Rivet Actor state, actions, and keys for a beginner. Include one simple application example.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Realtime Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Rivet Actors chat room with React clients, connection state, events, and access control. Identify the relevant examples.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Actor Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my actor design for lifecycle, input validation, error handling, persistence, and client usage. Recommend changes supported by this skill.

prompt_templates.title: Design Durable Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-actor workflow using queues, retries, SQLite, and orchestration. Include security boundaries, failure handling, and migration considerations.

output_examples.input: How should I model a chat room?
output_examples.output: Use one actor per room. Store room state in the actor, identify rooms with keys, and authorize each connection before publishing events.

output_examples.input: How can a React client receive updates?
output: Create the typed React client with the trusted actor endpoint.
Resolve the actor by its stable key.
Subscribe to events and remove listeners during cleanup.

output_examples.input: What should a durable order workflow include?
output_examples.output: Use queued work, idempotent workflow steps, explicit error handling, persisted state, and versioned SQLite migrations. Validate every external destination before requests.

best_practices: Use stable actor keys that match domain ownership and access boundaries.
Validate connection parameters, action inputs, external URLs, and permissions before processing.
Use production authentication libraries, trusted endpoints, and environment-managed secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not accept unsigned tokens or placeholder validators in production.
Do not fetch user-controlled URLs without an allowlist and network restrictions.
Do not embed production tokens or private endpoints in client examples.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Rivet Actors concepts, TypeScript clients, lifecycle, realtime events, workflows, storage, authentication, configuration, and deployment guidance.

faq.question: Does it deploy an application?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples, while deployment still requires your Rivet environment and tooling.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Treat them as learning templates. Replace placeholders, validate inputs, review security, and test behavior before production use.

faq.question: Which client environments are documented?
faq.answer: The material includes JavaScript, React, HTTP, WebSocket, Cloudflare, backend, and other framework integration examples.

faq.question: Does it include persistence patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes in-memory state, KV storage, SQLite operations, queues, synchronization, and migration examples.

faq.question: Are authentication examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Some validators are intentionally simplified, so use proven libraries and complete signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and permission checks.
